sections.h2: Who do Fleming County owners deal with on property tax?
sections.html:
Two courthouse-square offices carry most of the load, and a third takes over when a bill goes bad. The PVA answers value questions at 606-845-1401, and the county's PVA page lists weekday opening from 8 until 4:30. The sheriff bills and collects at 201 Court Square in Flemingsburg, with phones answered at 606-845-4701 (press 1) from 8 until 4:30 Monday to Friday. Once a bill is delinquent, the county clerk handles it.

It helps to know what the PVA will not do. By its own description, the office appraises property at fair cash value, maintains tax maps and ownership records and processes exemptions, but it neither writes laws nor sets rates. Rates come from the fiscal court, city councils, the school board and other districts. The fiscal court itself meets at the courthouse, 100 Court Square, on the second Tuesday of every month at 9 a.m. Eastern.

A PVA or deputy walks each property at least once in four years and may measure the outside of a building whether or not the owner is in. Send the PVA any new mailing address in writing so notices do not go astray.

sections.h2: What does the Fleming County tax year look like?
sections.html:
Fleming runs the standard Kentucky calendar, which opens October 1. Statements usually leave the sheriff's office near the end of September. A missing bill changes nothing about the debt, so owners without one phone 606-845-4701 and ask for the balance, or use the sheriff's online tax record search.

The 2026 discount window closed on November 1, 2026, and the face amount applies through December 31. The sheriff's example makes the stakes plain: a $1,000 bill costs $980 inside the discount window, $1,000 afterward, and $1,210 by February.

  • Counter payments are cash, a check payable to the Fleming County Sheriff, or a money order.
  • Cards work at the counter or by phone and add a 2.5 percent service charge.
  • Mail must carry a postmark on or before the deadline.
  • A drop box at the sheriff's door stays open at all hours and is emptied at 8 each morning under camera watch.

sections.h2: How does a Fleming County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA, because the board will not hear anyone who skipped that step. Kentucky opens the tax roll for inspection for thirteen days beginning the first Monday of May. A conference during that stretch keeps the right to file with the county clerk alive until the next business day after the stretch ends. The Department of Revenue's illustration: inspection from May 3 to May 17 means the clerk must have the paper by the close of May 18.

After that, the local board of assessment appeals convenes 25 to 35 days later. Bring paper. The board turns down any appeal lacking insurance policies, building costs, sale listings or similar proof.

  • At the conference the PVA must walk you through how the value was reached and record the result.
  • A paid agent must hold one of the credentials the state lists, such as attorney, CPA or licensed appraiser, and show your signed authorization.
  • Hearings may be audio-recorded by the taxpayer.

The sheriff will redirect any value complaint to the PVA. Filing and then missing the hearing closes the door to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Is a homestead exemption worth claiming in Fleming County?
sections.html:
For a qualifying owner it is worth claiming. The state deducts $49,100 from the assessed value of the home on the 2025 and 2026 rolls, and the tax is figured on what remains. Fleming County's typical owner-occupied house is valued at $134,700 by the Census Bureau, which would leave $85,600 taxable.

The PVA takes the form. Owners show their age with a birth certificate, license, passport or comparable record. Total disability must be certified by a federal agency or a retirement system, with benefits paid across the entire year, and most such claims have to be re-filed each year; veterans with service-connected disabilities and people found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from that requirement.

If a lender pays the tax from escrow, the sheriff still expects the owner to confirm that it was paid on time. Check the sheriff's record search after the discount period closes.

sections.h2: What happens with Fleming County taxes when a house sells?
sections.html:
The tax follows ownership, and the sheriff will talk through proration for any buyer or seller who calls with a closing date. Under KRS 134.015 the tax is the owner's own debt from the assessment date, and under KRS 134.420 a lien on an unpaid parcel can stay for 11 years after a sale. A sensible order of events: get the balance from the sheriff before listing, then have the closing agent settle the year's bill.

When the sheriff's office closes on April 15, whatever is unpaid goes to the Fleming County Clerk under KRS 134.122. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, commissions and a lien fee follow, and the county attorney writes the owner twice. The clerk then holds a sale between 90 and 135 days after the transfer.

The deed also carries a state transfer tax, which the seller pays. It equals $0.50 per $500 of price, so a sale at the county's median value of $134,700 costs $135.00; the 270th block of $500 is only partly filled but counts in full.

Ask the clerk's office in Flemingsburg for any payoff on a transferred bill, and tell the PVA about a new mailing address after closing.

sections.h2: What is the setting for a Fleming County house sale?
sections.html:
Fleming County was cut from Mason County in 1798 and named for Colonel John Fleming. Flemingsburg is the seat, Ewing is the second city and Elizaville is a census-designated place. The county measures 351 square miles, 349 of them land, and borders Mason, Lewis, Rowan, Bath, Nicholas and Robertson counties. The General Assembly gave it the title Covered Bridge Capital of Kentucky in 1998, and the county's courthouse was replaced in 1830 and again in 1952. The 2020 count classed every resident as rural.

Census QuickFacts adds some numbers sellers can use:

  • 15,787 residents in 2025, up 4.7 percent from 2020.
  • 74.8 percent of housing occupied by its owner, across 5,859 households.
  • Typical home value of $134,700 and typical monthly rent of $715.
  • Household income of $49,307 at the median.
  • A commute of 33.1 minutes on average.
  • No building permits issued in 2025.

Without new construction, nearly every buyer is shopping among older houses, so condition matters. A seller who owes taxes or faces repairs can weigh the cost of fixing up a listing against an as-is cash offer.

faqs.q: When do Fleming County tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: Statements typically go out at the end of September. In 2026 the 2 percent discount period began October 1, and an owner who has no bill by then can call 606-845-4701 and press 1.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost in Fleming County?
faqs.a: January adds 5 percent. From February 1 to April 15 the total reaches 121 percent of the bill, and anything unpaid after that goes to the county clerk.

faqs.q: Where is the Fleming County Sheriff's tax counter?
faqs.a: 201 Court Square in Flemingsburg, open weekdays from 8 until 4:30. A drop box at the entrance takes payments around the clock.

faqs.q: Who changes a Fleming County property value?
faqs.a: Only the PVA can, at 606-845-1401. The sheriff cannot alter an assessment, and a PVA conference has to come before any appeal.

faqs.q: Who gets the Fleming County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Homeowners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and live in the house. It removes $49,100 from the value on the 2025 and 2026 rolls.
